Let's dive into Chapter 5: Navigating Self-Promotion—Staying Authentic and Avoiding “Human Spam.”
If you’re putting your work out there, you’ve probably wondered—how do you share what you’re creating without coming off as insincere, pushy, or just a little too self-focused?
It’s a tricky balance, right? On one hand, you want your work to be seen. On the other, nobody wants to be that person—the relentless self-promoter clogging up everyone’s feed.
So, how do you stay visible and authentic at the same time?
Here’s the thing: self-promotion doesn’t have to feel awkward or forced. If you approach it as a natural extension of your creative journey, it can actually feel pretty good. Think of it less as advertising and more as sharing your story, your process, or even the lessons you’ve picked up along the way.
At its heart, authentic self-promotion is about generosity. It’s not just about broadcasting your wins—it’s about offering something meaningful to others. Maybe that’s a helpful resource, a behind-the-scenes look, or a story that others can learn from.
When you focus on contributing to your community, rather than chasing likes or validation, people pick up on that. It feels genuine. And guess what? Folks are far more likely to pay attention.
To avoid turning into “human spam,” be selective about what you share. Not every milestone needs a megaphone. Instead, look for those moments that truly offer value—like a breakthrough, a lesson learned, or an invitation to join in something creative.
Another big one? Make it a two-way street. Don’t just talk at your audience—talk with them. Ask for feedback. Respond to comments. Invite collaboration. That back-and-forth is what builds trust and makes your work feel more like a conversation than a monologue.
Imagine you’re a writer launching a new book. You could just blast out post after post about your release date… but what if you took folks behind the scenes instead? Maybe you share the ups and downs of getting the book done, or the resources that inspired you. That kind of honesty draws people in—they feel like they’re part of the journey, not just an audience.
Here are a few practical tips to keep your self-promotion feeling real:
First, share with intention—not just because you feel like you have to. Focus on what’s meaningful and relevant, both to you and your community.
Second, quality over quantity. Thoughtful, well-crafted updates are way more powerful than a constant stream of shallow posts.
And finally, listen as much as you share. Pay attention to what your audience cares about. Their needs and interests matter just as much as your own.
When you see self-promotion as a way to serve and connect, you naturally build visibility—without sacrificing your integrity. The goal isn’t to be the loudest voice in the room. It’s to add something meaningful to the conversation.
Over time, this approach draws in people who are genuinely interested in your work—and who want to stick around for the long haul.
So, finding the right balance is an ongoing process. It takes self-awareness, empathy, and a willingness to adjust as you go. But if you stay true to your values and keep the focus on others, you’ll build a presence that feels both authentic and impactful.
